questions.question: What will be the ratio of simple interest earned on a certain sum at the same rate percentage p.a. for 4 years and that for 6 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the Principal and Rate of interest are the same, Simple Interest is directly proportional to Time.

SI ∝ T

Ratio of SI = T₁ : T₂

Ratio of SI = 4 : 6

Ratio of SI = 2 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the Principal = P

Let the Rate of Interest = R% p.a.

Time period 1 (T₁) = 4 years

Time period 2 (T₂) = 6 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8674fbbec7fbbd2e26589ad4751d52f51ea384728d02ce2c9f83fdeda364a6cb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest for 4 years (SI₁) = (P × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ Simple Interest for 6 years (SI₂) = (P × R × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ Ratio = SI₁ : SI₂

⇒ Ratio = [(P × R × 4) ÷ 100] : [(P × R × 6) ÷ 100]

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 6

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal sum. The interest earned every year remains constant. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Proportionality Rules in SI

When Principal and Rate are fixed, SI is directly proportional to Time. Similarly, when Principal and Time are fixed, SI is directly proportional to the Rate.

Sum Doubling Time

For a sum to double itself under simple interest, the accumulated interest must be equal to the principal amount. The required time can be found directly using T = 100 ÷ R.

Amount Calculation

The total accumulated amount at the end of the time period is the sum of the Principal and Simple Interest. Formula: A = P(1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

questions.question: Alex invested $1500 in a savings bond with a simple interest rate of 6% per annum. How much interest will he receive after 4 years?
questions.solution:
Here is the solution in HTML format:

**Given:**

Principal (P) = $1500

Rate of interest (R) = 6% per annum

Time period (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

**Calculation:**

SI = (1500 × 6 × 4) / 100

⇒ SI = (1500 × 24) / 100

⇒ SI = 36000 / 100

⇒ SI = 360

The interest Alex will receive after 4 years is $360.

questions.question: The difference between simple interest on a certain sum at the annual rate of 10 percent for 7 years and 8 years is Rs. 57. What is the sum?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Annual rate of simple interest = 10%

Difference in interest for 7 years and 8 years = Rs. 57

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Principal (P) × Rate (R) × Time (T) / 100

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be P.

SI for 7 years = P × 10 × 7 / 100

SI for 8 years = P × 10 × 8 / 100

Difference in SI = SI for 8 years - SI for 7 years

⇒ P × 10 × 8 / 100 - P × 10 × 7 / 100 = 57

⇒ P × 10 × (8 - 7) / 100 = 57

⇒ P × 10 × 1 / 100 = 57

⇒ P × 10 / 100 = 57

⇒ P / 10 = 57

⇒ P = 57 × 10

⇒ P = 570

**The sum is Rs. 570.**
